content_blocks.steps_heading: Your Path to CAPM Certification in Frisco

steps_items.heading: Confirm Your Eligibility
steps_items.text: CAPM requires a secondary degree (high school diploma, associate, or equivalent) and completion of formal project management education—but no prior work experience. This makes CAPM ideal for career-changers and early-stage professionals entering Frisco's project-driven employers.

steps_items.heading: Complete 23 Hours of Instruction
steps_items.text: Enroll in Granite PM Academy's live-virtual, instructor-led boot camp. Our intensive format compresses the required contact hours into a focused schedule, letting you balance certification study with your current role while preparing thoroughly for exam success.

steps_items.heading: Submit Your PMI Application
steps_items.text: After course completion, register with PMI and submit your CAPM application along with the exam fee. Our team provides guidance on the application process so you can move forward with confidence and clarity.

steps_items.heading: Prepare and Test
steps_items.text: Use Granite PM Academy's exam-preparation resources—including practice exams and targeted review—to solidify your knowledge. Then schedule and sit for the CAPM exam, validated by PMI's rigorous standards and recognized across Frisco's leading organizations.

steps_items.heading: Maintain Your Credential
steps_items.text: CAPM certification lasts three years. Maintain your credential by earning professional development units (PDUs) through ongoing education, project work, or professional activities. Renewal keeps your certification current and your skills competitive in your local job market.

fq_items.question: Do I need project management experience to take the CAPM?
fq_items.answer: No prior PM experience is required. The CAPM only requires secondary education (high school diploma or equivalent) and 23 contact hours of project management education — which our course fulfills.

fq_items.question: How does the CAPM differ from the PMP?
fq_items.answer: The PMP requires 36–60 months of project leadership experience; the CAPM does not. Many professionals earn the CAPM early in their career, gain experience, then pursue the PMP.
